steps.instruction: Put a large saucepan of water on to boil.
Finely chop the 100g pancetta, having first removed any rind. Finely grate 50g pecorino cheese and 50g parmesan and mix them together.
Beat the 3 large eggs in a medium bowl and season with a little freshly grated black pepper. Set everything aside.
Add 1 tsp salt to the boiling water, add 350g spaghetti and when the water comes back to the boil, cook at a constant simmer, covered, for 10 minutes or until al dente (just cooked).
Squash 2 peeled plump garlic cloves with the blade of a knife, just to bruise it.
While the spaghetti is cooking, fry the pancetta with the garlic. Drop 50g unsalted butter into a large frying pan or wok and, as soon as the butter has melted, tip in the pancetta and garlic.
Leave to cook on a medium heat for about 5 minutes, stirring often, until the pancetta is golden and crisp. The garlic has now imparted its flavour, so take it out with a slotted spoon and discard.

Keep the heat under the pancetta on low. When the pasta is ready, lift it from the water with a pasta fork or tongs and put it in the frying pan with the pancetta. Don’t worry if a little water drops in the pan as well (you want this to happen) and don’t throw the pasta water away yet.
Mix most of the cheese in with the eggs, keeping a small handful back for sprinkling over later.

Take the pan of spaghetti and pancetta off the heat. Now quickly pour in the eggs and cheese. Using the tongs or a long fork, lift up the spaghetti so it mixes easily with the egg mixture, which thickens but doesn’t scramble, and everything is coated.
Add extra pasta cooking water to keep it saucy (several tablespoons should do it). You don’t want it wet, just moist. Season with a little salt, if needed.

Use a long-pronged fork to twist the pasta on to the serving plate or bowl. Serve immediately with a little sprinkling of the remaining cheese and a grating of black pepper. If the dish does get a little dry before serving, splash in some more hot pasta water and the glossy sauciness will be revived.

steps.instruction: Bring salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Cook the guanciale with 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium heat, stirring frequently, until the fat renders and the pork is crisp.
In a large metal heatproof bowl, whisk whole eggs, yolks, Pecorino, Parmigiano and black pepper.
Transfer pasta to the pork skillet without draining the pasta pot, add remaining olive oil, cool slightly, then scrape pasta, pork and fat into the egg mixture; mix in 1/2 cup pasta water.
Set the bowl over the pot of boiling pasta water without letting it touch the water; stir quickly with tongs until the sauce is creamy, silky and leaves trails, then serve immediately.

technique: Use mostly yolks with some whole eggs for a rich but balanced sauce.
Use equal Pecorino Romano and Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Finish in a makeshift double boiler, stirring constantly, to thicken the eggs without curdling.
tips: Do not oversalt the pasta water because the pork and cheeses are salty.
Serve immediately because the egg sauce continues to thicken as it sits.

- Kosher salt
- 1 pound (450 g) dried spaghetti
- 1/2 cup diced guanciale, pancetta, or bacon (about 3 ounces; 85 g)
- 3 tablespoons (45 ml) extra-virgin olive oil, divided
- 2 whole large eggs plus 6 yolks

- 1/4 cup grated Parmigiano-Reggiano (25 g), plus more for serving
- 1 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, plus more for serving

菜名：意式培根蛋面
1. Bring salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.【high heat】
2. Cook the guanciale with 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium heat, stirring frequently, until the fat renders and the pork is crisp.（about 7 minutes）【medium heat】
3. In a large metal heatproof bowl, whisk whole eggs, yolks, Pecorino, Parmigiano and black pepper.
4. Transfer pasta to the pork skillet without draining the pasta pot, add remaining olive oil, cool slightly, then scrape pasta, pork and fat into the egg mixture; mix in 1/2 cup pasta water.
5. Set the bowl over the pot of boiling pasta water without letting it touch the water; stir quickly with tongs until the sauce is creamy, silky and leaves trails, then serve immediately.【gentle steam heat】
